These\n//    trials are independent (they only read `clustered` and `points`), so they\n//    are distributed across OpenMP threads with dynamic scheduling.\n//  * Each candidate-cluster growth keeps a per-candidate running maximum\n//    distance to the current members, updated incrementally whenever a member\n//    is added. This yields exactly the same values as recomputing the maximum\n//    over all members (max is exact in floating point), and reduces the cost\n//    per added member from O(N * |members|) to O(N).\n//  * The selection of the best seed (largest cardinality, ties broken by the\n//    smallest seed index, as in the sequential scan) is a deterministic\n//    reduction, so results are bit-identical to the sequential program.\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <limits>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <omp.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nstatic const double MAX_WIDTH = 20.0;\nstatic const double MAX_HEIGHT = 20.0;\n\n// Structure to represent a point in 2D space\nstruct Point {\n    double x, y;\n};\n\n// Structure to represent a cluster\nstruct Cluster {\n    std::vector<int> members;\n    int seed_point;\n};\n\n// Generate synthetic 2D point data in clusters\nvoid generateSyntheticData(std::vector<Point>& points, const int N, unsigned int seed = 42) {\n    auto frand = [&seed]() mutable { return rand_r(&seed) / static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX); };\n    \n    const double min_dim = std::min(MAX_WIDTH, MAX_HEIGHT);\n    int count = 0;\n    \n    while (count < N) {\n        // Create group_cnt points within a circle of radius R\n        // around center point (cntr_x, cntr_y)\n        const double cntr_x = frand() * MAX_WIDTH;\n        const double cntr_y = frand() * MAX_HEIGHT;\n        const double R = frand() * min_dim / 2.0;\n        int group_cnt = static_cast<int>(frand() * (N / 30.0));\n        \n        // Make sure we don't make more points than we need\n        if (group_cnt > (N - count)) {\n            group_cnt = N - count;\n        }\n        \n        while (group_cnt > 0) {\n            const double sign = (frand() < 0.5) ? -1.0 : 1.0;\n            const double r = frand() * R;\n            const double dx = (2.0 * frand() - 1.0) * r;\n            const double dy = std::sqrt(r * r - dx * dx) * sign;\n            const double x = cntr_x + dx;\n            const double y = cntr_y + dy;\n            \n            if (x < 0 || x > MAX_WIDTH || y < 0 || y > MAX_HEIGHT) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            \n            points[count] = {x, y};\n            count++;\n            group_cnt--;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Calculate Euclidean distance between two points\ninline double distance(const Point& p1, const Point& p2) {\n    double dx = p1.x - p2.x;\n    double dy = p1.y - p2.y;\n    return std::sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);\n}\n\n// Per-thread scratch storage for candidate cluster generation, reused across\n// seeds to avoid repeated allocation.\nstruct CandidateWorkspace {\n    std::vector<int> cand;        // Indices of still-eligible candidate points\n    std::vector<double> max_dist; // Running max distance from candidate to members\n    std::vector<int> members;     // Members of the candidate cluster being built\n};\n\n// Generate a candidate cluster starting from a seed point.\n// `unclustered` lists all currently unclustered point indices in ascending order.\n// Returns the cardinality (size) of the cluster; members are left in ws.members.\n//\n// Semantics are identical to the sequential version: at each step, the eligible\n// candidate (not clustered, not already a member) with the smallest maximum\n// distance to all current members is added, provided that distance is below the\n// threshold. Ties are broken by the lowest point index.\nstatic int generateCandidateCluster(const int seed_point,\n                                    const std::vector<int>& unclustered,\n                                    const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                                    const double threshold,\n                                    CandidateWorkspace& ws) {\n    std::vector<int>& cand = ws.cand;\n    std::vector<double>& max_dist = ws.max_dist;\n    std::vector<int>& members = ws.members;\n\n    const int n_uncl = static_cast<int>(unclustered.size());\n    cand.resize(n_uncl);\n    max_dist.resize(n_uncl);\n    members.clear();\n    members.push_back(seed_point);\n\n    // Initialize the candidate set with every unclustered point except the\n    // seed, and the running maximum distance with the distance to the seed.\n    // Candidates that can never be added (distance >= threshold) are dropped\n    // immediately: their running maximum can only grow.\n    const Point ps = points[seed_point];\n    int n_cand = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_uncl; ++i) {\n        const int c = unclustered[i];\n        if (c == seed_point) continue;\n        const double d = distance(points[c], ps);\n        if (d < threshold) {\n            cand[n_cand] = c;\n            max_dist[n_cand] = d;\n            ++n_cand;\n        }\n    }\n\n    while (n_cand > 0) {\n        // Find the candidate with the smallest running maximum distance.\n        // Candidates are kept in ascending index order, and the strict '<'\n        // reproduces the first-minimum tie-breaking of the sequential scan.\n        int best = 0;\n        double best_d = max_dist[0];\n        for (int i = 1; i < n_cand; ++i) {\n            const double d = max_dist[i];\n            if (d < best_d) {\n                best_d = d;\n                best = i;\n            }\n        }\n\n        const int closest = cand[best];\n        members.push_back(closest);\n        const Point pc = points[closest];\n\n        // Update running maxima against the new member, compacting the\n        // candidate list: remove the chosen point and any point whose running\n        // maximum reached the threshold (it can never be added later).\n        int w = 0;\n        for (int i = 0; i < n_cand; ++i) {\n            if (i == best) continue;\n            const double d = distance(points[cand[i]], pc);\n            const double m = std::max(max_dist[i], d);\n            if (m < threshold) {\n                cand[w] = cand[i];\n                max_dist[w] = m;\n                ++w;\n            }\n        }\n        n_cand = w;\n    }\n\n    return static_cast<int>(members.size());\n}\n\n// Main QT clustering algorithm\nstd::vector<Cluster> qtClustering(const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                                  const double threshold) {\n    const int N = static_cast<int>(points.size());\n    std::vector<char> clustered(N, 0);\n    std::vector<int> unclustered_indices;\n    std::vector<Cluster> clusters;\n    \n    // Initialize unclustered indices\n    unclustered_indices.reserve(N);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) {\n        unclustered_indices.push_back(i);\n    }\n\n    const int num_threads = omp_get_max_threads();\n    std::vector<CandidateWorkspace> workspaces(num_threads);\n    for (auto& ws : workspaces) {\n        ws.cand.reserve(N);\n        ws.max_dist.reserve(N);\n        ws.members.reserve(N);\n    }\n\n    // Per-thread best results, merged deterministically after each round.\n    std::vector<int> thread_best_card(num_threads);\n    std::vector<int> thread_best_seed(num_threads);\n    std::vector<std::vector<int>> thread_best_members(num_threads);\n    \n    // Main clustering loop\n    while (!unclustered_indices.empty()) {\n        const int n_uncl = static_cast<int>(unclustered_indices.size());\n\n        // Try each unclustered point as a seed, in parallel. Each thread\n        // tracks its best (largest cardinality; ties -> smallest seed index).\n        #pragma omp parallel num_threads(num_threads)\n        {\n            const int tid = omp_get_thread_num();\n            CandidateWorkspace& ws = workspaces[tid];\n            int local_card = -1;\n            int local_seed = -1;\n            std::vector<int>& local_members = thread_best_members[tid];\n            local_members.clear();\n\n            #pragma omp for schedule(dynamic, 1) nowait\n            for (int i = 0; i < n_uncl; ++i) {\n                const int seed = unclustered_indices[i];\n                const int cardinality = generateCandidateCluster(\n                    seed, unclustered_indices, points, threshold, ws);\n\n                if (cardinality > local_card ||\n                    (cardinality == local_card && seed < local_seed)) {\n                    local_card = cardinality;\n                    local_seed = seed;\n                    local_members.swap(ws.members);\n                }\n            }\n\n            thread_best_card[tid] = local_card;\n            thread_best_seed[tid] = local_seed;\n        }\n\n        // Deterministic reduction across threads: largest cardinality, then\n        // smallest seed index (equivalent to the sequential first-max scan).\n        int max_cardinality = -1;\n        int best_seed = -1;\n        int best_tid = -1;\n        for (int t = 0; i < best_cluster_members.size(); ++i) {\n                clustered[best_cluster_members[i]] = 1;\n            }\n            \n            // Remove clustered points from unclustered list\n            unclustered_indices.erase(\n                std::remove_if(unclustered_indices.begin(), unclustered_indices.end(),\n                              [&clustered](int idx) { return clustered[idx] != 0; }),\n                unclustered_indices.end()\n            );\n        } else {\n            // No more clusters can be formed\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return clusters;\n}\n\n// Validation: check that clusters satisfy the QT clustering properties\nbool validateClusters(const std::vector<Cluster>& clusters,\n                     const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                     const double threshold) {\n    bool valid = true;\n    \n    printf(\"Validating clusters:\\n\");\n    \n    // Check each cluster\n    for (size_t c = 0; c < clusters.size(); ++c) {\n        const auto& cluster = clusters[c];\n        double max_diameter = 0.0;\n        \n        // Check diameter (max distance between any two points)\n        const int n = static_cast<int>(cluster.members.size());\n        #pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 16) reduction(max : max_diameter)\n        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n            for (int j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n                const double dist = distance(points[cluster.members[i]], \n                                           points[cluster.members[j]]);\n                max_diameter = std::max(max_diameter, dist);\n            }\n        }\n        \n        if (c < 10) { // Print first 10 clusters\n            printf(\"  Cluster %zu: size=%zu, seed=%d, diameter=%.4f\\n\", \n                   c, cluster.members.size(), cluster.seed_point, max_diameter);\n        }\n        \n        // Validate diameter is within threshold\n        if (max_diameter > threshold * 1.001) { // Allow small numerical error\n            printf(\"ERROR: Cluster %zu has diameter %.4f > threshold %.4f\\n\", \n                   c, max_diameter, threshold);\n            valid = false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Check for duplicate memberships\n    std::vector<int> membership(points.size(), -1);\n    for (size_t c = 0; c < clusters.size(); ++c) {\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < clusters[c].members.size(); ++i) {\n            const int member = clusters[c].members[i];\n            if (membership[member] >= 0) {\n                printf(\"ERROR: Point %d appears in multiple clusters (%d and %zu)\\n\",\n                       member, membership[member], c);\n                valid = false;\n            }\n            membership[member] = static_cast<int>(c);\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Count clustered points\n    int clustered_count = 0;\n    for (size_t i = 0; Candidates whose running maximum reaches\n// the threshold can never be added (the maximum only grows); they are marked\n// dead (+inf) and physically compacted out of the arrays only now and then.\nstatic int generateCandidateCluster(const int seed_point,\n                                    const std::vector<int>& unclustered,\n                                    const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                                    const double threshold,\n                                    CandidateWorkspace& ws) {\n    const double INF = std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();\n    std::vector<int>& cand = ws.cand;\n    std::vector<double>& cx = ws.cx;\n    std::vector<double>& cy = ws.cy;\n    std::vector<double>& max_dist = ws.max_dist;\n    std::vector<int>& members = ws.members;\n\n    const int n_uncl = static_cast<int>(unclustered.size());\n    cand.resize(n_uncl);\n    cx.resize(n_uncl);\n    cy.resize(n_uncl);\n    max_dist.resize(n_uncl);\n    members.clear();\n    members.push_back(seed_point);\n\n    // Initialize the candidate set with every unclustered point except the\n    // seed that lies within the threshold of the seed, in ascending order.\n    const Point ps = points[seed_point];\n    int n_cand = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; m : INF;\n            newly_dead += alive ? 0 : 1;\n        }\n        n_dead = newly_dead; // Counts every dead entry (old ones stay +inf)\n\n        // Compact once a good fraction of the entries are dead.\n        if (n_dead > (n_cand >> 2)) {\n            int w = 0;\n            for (int i = 0; i < n_cand; ++i) {\n                if (md_p[i] != INF) {\n                    cand_p[w] = cand_p[i];\n                    cx_p[w] = cx_p[i];\n                    cy_p[w] = cy_p[i];\n                    md_p[w] = md_p[i];\n                    ++w;\n                }\n            }\n            n_cand = w;\n            n_dead = 0;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return static_cast<int>(members.size());\n}\n\n'''\ns=s[:start]+new+s[end:]\ns=s.replace('''        ws.cand.reserve(N);\n        ws.max_dist.reserve(N);''','''        ws.cand.reserve(N);\n        ws.cx.reserve(N);\n        ws.cy.reserve(N);\n        ws.max_dist.reserve(N);''')\n# thread configuration\ns=s.replace('#include <omp.h>\\n','#include <omp.h>\\n#include <sched.h>\\n')\ncfg='''\n// Parse a sysfs CPU list such as \"0,128\" or \"0-1,64-65\" and mark its entries.\nstatic void markCpuList(const char* list, std::vector<char>& seen) {\n    const char* p = list;\n    while (*p) {\n        char* end;\n        long a = strtol(p, &end, 10);\n        if (end == p) break;\n        long b = a;\n        p = end;\n        if (*p == '-') {\n            b = strtol(p + 1, &end, 10);\n            p = end;\n        }\n        for (long c = a; c <= b && c < static_cast<long>(seen.size()); ++c) {\n            if (c >= 0) seen[c] = 1;\n        }\n        if (*p == ',') ++p; else break;\n    }\n}\n\n// Choose the OpenMP team used for clustering. Fix: mallopt(M_MMAP_THRESHOLD 32MB, M_TRIM_THRESHOLD, M_TOP_PAD) plus a per-thread malloc(4MB)/free warm-up before timing.\n- GCC elides an unused malloc/free pair, so a warm-up must make the pointer observable (empty asm with \"r\"(ptr) and \"memory\" clobber).\n- Using all 256 hardware threads is much slower and very noisy for barrier-heavy loops; one pinned thread per physical core (via sched_setaffinity, parsing thread_siblings_list) is fastest and stable. OMP_PROC_BIND env works but the proc_bind clause alone is ignored by libgomp.\n\n**Why:** Each of these looked like an algorithmic problem at first and cost a lot of profiling time; perf has no kernel symbols here (kptr_restrict), strace -f -tt was the tool that revealed them.\n\n**How to apply:** For any future multithreaded benchmark on this box, check syscalls inside the timed region with strace first, warm up allocators outside timing, and default to physical cores.
